A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same OBCD research work. All 45 pages of each version, including figures, tables, equations and appendices, are readable and support comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original optimization experiments on sparse PCA, nonnegative PCA and nonlinear eigenvalue problems, including convergence plots and Tables 2–11.

after.justification: v2 reports original PCA experiments in Section 6 and Appendix J, including retained results and a new initialization comparison.

M1.justification: v2 retains the exact surrogate-based row update but removes v1's explicit OBCD-Approx branch and fifth-order iterative solver. It adds parallel pairwise Jacobi updates in Appendix C.4 and includes previously omitted cos(theta)=0 candidates in the breakpoint solver. The existing greedy working-set strategies remain.

E1.justification: The nonlinear-eigenvalue task evaluated in v1 Section 9.5 and Tables 9–11 is removed. The same ten datasets and three PCA tasks remain, with nonnegative and L1-based PCA relocated to Appendix J. The new initialization experiment does not introduce a new dataset or task.

E2.justification: Removing the nonlinear-eigenvalue comparison eliminates evaluated FOForth-GR, FOForth-P, FOForth-QR, OptM-QR and OptM-Cayley baselines. The retained PCA tables preserve their comparison structure and numerical entries, although PADM is now labeled SPM; that relabeling alone does not establish a newly evaluated algorithm.

E3.justification: v2 adds a comparison of identity and random baseline initializations with r=20, a 30-second budget and lambda values 10, 100, 1000 and 10000. This experiment reports cardinality using a 1e-6 threshold. Earlier shared-initialization PCA protocols remain in Appendix J; these additions do not establish that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: New Table 1 and Figure 1 investigate whether poor baseline performance persists under random versus identity initialization across ten datasets and four regularization strengths. This adds a substantive sensitivity analysis beyond v1's shared-initialization comparisons. Existing working-set and baseline-to-OBCD refinement analyses remain in Appendix J.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, experimental seeds, confidence intervals, variability estimates or significance tests. v2 clarifies the deterministic 10% improvement criterion for existing (+) annotations; this is not statistical uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: v2 adds initialization-comparison results and removes nonlinear-eigenvalue objective and gradient-residual results. For example, new Table 1 reports an MNIST objective gap of 6.25e+04 for OBCD-R(id), versus zero for LADMM(rnd), at r=20 and lambda=10. All numerical entries in corresponding retained PCA Tables 2–8 are unchanged.

T1.justification: v2 narrows row separability to coordinate-wise separability and adds explicit regularity and exact-solvability assumptions. It removes approximate block-stationarity theory, extends the hierarchy to global minimizers, revises the randomized iteration bound and adds a cyclic-selection theorem and proof. It also corrects the cardinality subdifferential and the breakpoint derivation's missing endpoint cases.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion newly claim that OBCD is the first greedy descent method with monotonicity for this problem class. The contribution scope shifts from explicit exact and approximate algorithms, including a fifth-order solver, toward globally solved subproblems and block-stationary solutions. The central feasibility and low-cost row-update claims remain.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive explanations of Cayley-method stagnation through toy examples, computational tradeoffs with full-gradient methods, and loss of stronger optimality when subproblems cannot be solved globally. It also interprets the new initialization results as evidence of escaping poor local minima. Earlier PCA working-set interpretations largely remain.

D1.justification: v2 documents the 1e-6 cardinality threshold and 10% table-annotation rule, expands the Jacobi-Givens-QR implementation, and describes incremental gradient computation. Code-access instructions change from author webpages to supplemental material, whose availability cannot be verified from the PDFs. Hardware, MATLAB/C++ implementation and the 1e-5 proximal parameter remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds deep-network application references, Chen's smoothing-method work and Chen et al.'s 2024 survey. It removes v1's Other Approaches discussion covering convex relaxations, penalties and second-order methods. Research positioning also shifts toward explicit priority claims about nonsmooth BCD and monotone greedy descent.

P1.justification: The abstract and substantial portions of the narrative are rewritten. Related work becomes an introduction subsection; application descriptions, greedy selection and supporting mathematics are redistributed. The appendix expands from an A–B organization to topic-specific Sections A–J, substantially changing how readers navigate the paper.

P2.justification: The main text changes from two columns to one. v2 adds the initialization table and plots and geometric-example Figure 2, converts the notation table into a list, and removes nonlinear-eigenvalue tables. Retained convergence plots are compressed and rearranged into different panel layouts rather than constituting new experimental results.

improvement.justification: v2 improves specific mathematical statements by correcting the cardinality subdifferential and missing breakpoint endpoints, and adds useful initialization controls and implementation explanations. However, its new cyclic proof infers stationarity at one iterate from update gaps across different iterates without establishing that connection (Appendix G.1, Equation 42). The parallel subproblem in Appendix C.4 also omits terms required by Lemma 2.4. These new theoretical gaps make the net quality benefit uncertain despite the concrete improvements.
